messages:
alejandra: Heads-up, seeing a sharp uptick in ECC/Xid on eu-central GPU pool starting ~06:10 UTC. Errors spiked, scheduler reports ~18% capacity unavailable. Some realtime jobs timed out. infra-bot: [automated] gpu-health-prober: 502 responses from 8/48 nodes in eu-central between 06:08-06:12 UTC. Aggregated XID_ERR rate: 4.8/s. samir: Is this correlated with the nightly firmware roll? I see a small patch landed last night to nvlink driver. rebecca: tagging oncall @oncall-rotation — can you confirm if drains kicked? oncall-rotation: I’m on it. Drains started automatically on 6 nodes, but several are flapping back to ready due to repeated soft ECC. Marcus, can you join for triage? marcus: joining. Quick check: probe logs on node eu-c-12 show repeated "Xid (0x4) - GPU reported a fault" and then a PCI reset. If resets fail we get stuck in partial-ready. samir: digging into metrics — the faulting nodes are all on rack eu-c-12b, same PSU vendor batch. Could be thermal/PSU causing retries. infra-bot: logs: ```
# Example from /var/log/gpu-prober.log
[06:09:21] Xid (0x4) detected on gpu0, vendor: NV
[06:09:22] Attempting soft reset
[06:09:22] PCIe reset returned EIO
[06:09:24] Marking device degraded
``` 
rebecca: Past incidents like this we quarantined whole rack and procced with replacement. Do we want to do that now or try targeted reboots? oncall-rotation: Reboots already attempted once; we still have 4 flapping nodes. Proposal: cordon the rack, migrate sched jobs to eu-west1 fallback, and open a swap ticket for PSU replacements. marcus: Agreed. Migration plan: 1) set autoscaling to allow temporary cross-region burst 2) pin latency-sensitive models to smaller replicas in eu-west1 to avoid tail latency 3) drain nodes with: ```rctl node drain eu-c-12b-0{3..8} --reason "soft ECC surge" --no-terminate``` samir: Will adjust routing policy to prefer eu-west1 for new requests, but existing sessions will fallback to smaller cap models to preserve correctness. Expect cost bump — estimate ~12% extra bandwidth egress. alejandra: Important: do not terminate GPUs until infra has confirmed HW swap path. We want to avoid accidental replacements. rebecca: I'll open hardware ticket with vendor and include serials from the 6 nodes. infra-bot: created ticket HW-12487, assigned to vendor-support, ETA initial triage 4 hours. oncall-rotation: Status update in 30m after migration metrics. If XID rate doesn't drop after draining the rack, we'll escalate to full rack replacement and start capacity re-provisioning. samir: I’ll push a quick probe update to lower aggressiveness of the prober to reduce false-positive drains while we validate firmware. marcus: I'll own the node-drain commands and verify no jobs are lost (we'll put a temporary hold on preemptible eviction). alejandra: Thanks all. Keep the thread for updates. :eyes:
